To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Heat stress during anther development and pollen maturation can cause a decrease in pollen viability and an increase in the percentage of abnormal pollen.

(1) Heat stress adversely affects fruitset in male-sterile tomatoes, especially when the heat stress is experienced by donor pollen, (2) Heat stress also adversely affects fruitset of male-fertile tomato plants, but to a lesser extent than in male-steriles, and (3) The effects of heat stress in male-sterilies can be reduced by using pollen that has not experienced heat stress.

(i) heat stress experienced by male and female reproductive structures of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) had similar adverse effects on fruit set, but (ii) the detrimental effect of heat stress on fruit set in male-sterile tomato was reduced if pollen was developed at a lower temperature
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of heat on pollen and ovule development in tomato.
the effect of temperature on pollen development in the anther and its subsequent fertilization of the ovule.
how heat stress affects the development and function of reproductive tissues of the tomato.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of heat on tomato reproduction are complex, and that the effects on pollen development, anther dehiscence, pollen germination, pollen tube growth and pollen tube competition are all important, and that these effects may vary depending on the temperature regime experienced by the male or female reproductive tissues.
pollen development is very sensitive to heat stress, and that this is a major factor in the reduction of fruitset in tomato and other crops at elevated temperatures.
heat stress experienced by pollen and anther tissues, but not by ovules, is a major cause of decreased fruit set in tomatoes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heat stress effects on fruitset in male-sterile tomato are largely due to heat stress experienced by pollen and anther tissues.
the effects of heat on pollen are much more important in reducing yield than are effects on ovules.
the effects of heat on fruit set in tomato are more severe than the effects on yield per fruit, but that both are reduced when pollen is produced at lower temperatures than the female tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of heat stress on tomato fruit set was not due to the effects of heat on ovule or embryo development, but rather due to the effect of heat on pollen development.
pollen development is more sensitive than ovule development to elevated growth temperature.
the effects of high temperature stress on male and on female reproduction in tomato are different.
